arch_note: arm64 is the default for new apps (owner answer Q4); the two lab examples keep x86_64.

lambda-web.network: No VPC. If a DB needs a VPC: S3/DynamoDB gateway endpoints (free) plus only the interface endpoints needed; no NAT
lambda-web.dr: backup-restore (IaC + ECR + state); pilot-light = ECR cross-region replication + IaC in a second region
lambda-web.cost: arm64 for new apps; HTTP API throttle as cost ceiling (Function URL when budget-first; CloudFront + WAF only when public and abuse-prone); Compute Savings Plan only when steady prod spend is known
lambda-web.sustainability: Scale to zero by design; arm64 (SUS05-BP02)

lambda-events.network: No VPC. If a DB needs a VPC: S3/DynamoDB gateway endpoints (free) plus only the interface endpoints needed; no NAT
lambda-events.dr: backup-restore (IaC + ECR + state); pilot-light = ECR cross-region replication + IaC in a second region
lambda-events.cost: arm64 for new apps; Compute Savings Plan only when steady prod spend is known
lambda-events.sustainability: Scale to zero by design; arm64 (SUS05-BP02)

ecs-fargate.network: Private subnets + VPC endpoints when few AZs and low egress; NAT when egress is broad (ask egress needs, COST08)
ecs-fargate.dr: backup-restore; warm-standby = scaled-down service in a second region
ecs-fargate.cost: arm64, Fargate Spot in dev only, Savings Plan for steady prod
ecs-fargate.sustainability: dev desired count 0 or destroy after the session

ec2-asg.dr: AMI + launch template in a second region (pilot light)
ec2-asg.cost: Graviton, Savings Plans, Spot in dev
ec2-asg.sustainability: Right-size with Compute Optimizer; ASG min 0 in dev

eks-workload.network: Shared cluster VPC; ALB via the Load Balancer Controller
eks-workload.dr: GitOps re-sync to a second cluster
eks-workload.cost: Shared cluster to amortize the control plane; Karpenter with Spot in dev
eks-workload.sustainability: Bin-packing on the shared cluster; arm64 node pools
